papers.title: In Search of the Viscosity Operator on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.scope: Survey and crosswalk for inequivalent geometric viscosity operators.

claims.statement: The rough/Bochner, Hodge, and deformation constructions are inequivalent in general on curved Riemannian manifolds.
claims.locator: Notices AMS 71(1), pp. 8-16, survey comparison of the candidate viscosity operators

assumptions.formal witness: a curved Riemannian setting on which the three operator maps are pairwise distinct
assumptions.convention: rough, Hodge, and deformation operators translated to analysis-positive-v1

papers.title: The formulation of the Navier-Stokes equations on Riemannian manifolds
papers.scope: Operator selection, stress, energy, hyperbolic obstruction, and relativistic limit.

claims.statement: For divergence-free velocity, L_Def = L_Hodge - 2 Ric in the positive convention.
claims.locator: Introduction, equations (1.1)-(1.3) and the divergence-free specialization immediately following (1.3)

claims.statement: On H2(-a^2), no positive absolute constant controls the expected global Hodge-Stokes energy estimate uniformly over all terminal times and weak solutions in the stated energy spaces.

assumptions.quantifier: no C0 > 0 works for every T > 0

claims.statement: The Lichnerowicz, Choquet-Bruhat, and Freistuehler-Temple first-order relativistic stresses all produce div(2 Def v) in the nonrelativistic spatial momentum equation.
claims.locator: arXiv:1608.05114v2, Section 5, especially equation (5.1) and the paragraph following it

papers.title: The restriction problem on the ellipsoid
papers.scope: Invariant restriction formula and its eccentricity expansion on an ellipsoid.

claims.statement: A projected ambient restriction gives an invariant ellipsoid viscosity candidate.
claims.locator: arXiv:2203.16050v1, Theorem 1.1, equations (1.4)--(1.5), with the component proof in Section 2

claims.statement: The candidate admits the stated expansion in ellipsoid eccentricity.

papers.title: The Gauss formulas for Laplacians on submanifolds
papers.scope: Gauss formulas for vector Laplacians on submanifolds of arbitrary codimension.

claims.statement: The intrinsic Ricci tensor equals its Euclidean Gauss-equation expression.
Bochner and Hodge Laplacians admit the paper's arbitrary-codimension formulas.

papers.title: Thin shell limit and the derivation of the viscosity operator on the ellipsoid
papers.scope: Four scaling-direction candidates under Navier and Hodge wall conditions.

claims.statement: The four ellipsoid candidates collapse to their Navier/Hodge endpoints on a sphere.
claims.locator: arXiv:2511.10579v1, Theorems 1.1 and 1.3, formulas (1.4)--(1.7), specialized by Remark 1.5

claims.statement: The scaling-direction thin-shell result depends on the averaging prescription.
claims.locator: arXiv:2511.10579v1, Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.6 with Remark 1.8; the paper labels these limits heuristic

papers.title: Resolving the viscosity operator ambiguity on Riemannian manifolds via a kinematic selection principle
papers.scope: Intrinsic strain selection, hyperbolic coercivity, weak solutions, and energy decay.

claims.statement: The metric rate under a velocity field is twice the deformation tensor.

On a complete noncompact two-dimensional manifold of bounded geometry with K <= -kappa^2 < 0, for every mu > 0 and u0 in H, the deformation-viscosity Navier-Stokes equation has a unique global weak solution in L-infinity(0,T;H) intersect L2(0,T;V) for every T > 0, admits a pressure distribution recovering momentum, and satisfies ||u(t)||_L2^2 <= exp(-2 mu kappa^2 t) ||u0||_L2^2.
claims.locator: arXiv:2605.17502v2, Theorem 6.1, equations (39)-(40), with uniqueness detailed in Remark 6.2

assumptions.manifold: complete, noncompact, two-dimensional Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry
assumptions.curvature: Gaussian curvature K <= -kappa^2 < 0 for some kappa > 0
assumptions.spaces: H and V are the L2 and H1 closures of smooth compactly supported divergence-free vector fields

papers.title: Boundary conditions select the viscous operator on Riemannian hypersurfaces: formal analysis and rigorous thin-shell limits
papers.scope: Wall-condition selection, matched fields, and rigorous thin-shell convergence.

claims.statement: The tangential ambient operator gives L_Def + 2a Ric + 4a(1-a)S^2.
claims.locator: arXiv:2605.20589v3, Lemma 3.1, Proposition 3.2, and Theorem 3.3, equations (12)--(18)

claims.statement: A finite-thickness tangential profile satisfies both wall laws.

For torus-type surfaces of revolution and for both stress-free/deformation and vorticity-free/Hodge wall conditions, the thin-shell forms Mosco-converge; the associated nonnegative self-adjoint operators have strongly convergent resolvents and semigroups uniformly on compact time intervals; eigenvalues converge with multiplicity on each fixed azimuthal mode and, by the uniform high-mode gap, for the full spectrum without spectral pollution.

assumptions.spectral scope: fixed-mode and full-spectrum convergence with multiplicity; no high-mode pollution

claims.statement: A resolved curved 3D shell converges after transverse averaging to the selected surface operator, with mesh convergence at fixed thickness established separately from thickness convergence.
claims.locator: Project numerical gate motivated by arXiv:2605.20589v3, Theorem 4.5; not a numerical theorem asserted in the paper

assumptions.required limits: mesh size h -> 0 at fixed epsilon, then thickness epsilon -> 0
assumptions.geometry: resolved curved volume shell rather than a normal-fibre surrogate

papers.title: Non-uniqueness of the Leray-Hopf solutions in the hyperbolic setting
papers.scope: Weak-solution nonuniqueness and Liouville failure on hyperbolic space.

claims.statement: The computational H2 model has scalar curvature -2a^2.
claims.locator: arXiv:1006.2819v1, Section 2.1, constant-curvature identities specialized to H2(-a^2)

claims.statement: For every a > 0, the deformation-viscosity Navier-Stokes equation on H2(-a^2) admits distinct Leray-Hopf solutions with the same initial datum.

assumptions.viscosity: 2 Def* Def, equivalently the paper's N-S_H2(-a^2)

papers.title: Liouville theorems for the Stationary Navier Stokes equation on a hyperbolic space
papers.scope: Stationary Navier--Stokes Liouville theorems on hyperbolic spaces.

claims.statement: A smooth divergence-free finite-Dirichlet stationary deformation-viscosity solution on HN(-a^2) vanishes for N=3,4; for N=2, an additional L-infinity bound makes it an L2 harmonic gradient; and for N>=5, the same bound implies vanishing.

assumptions.equation: 2 Def* Def u + nabla_u u + dp = 0, d* u = 0
assumptions.base regularity: smooth velocity and pressure; finite Dirichlet integral
assumptions.extra bound: u in L-infinity for N=2 and N>=5 only

papers.title: Antithesis of the Stokes paradox on the hyperbolic plane
papers.scope: Nontrivial steady Stokes and Navier--Stokes flows on a hyperbolic exterior domain.

claims.statement: For every R0,a > 0, the exterior of the radius-R0 geodesic ball in H2(-a^2) admits a nontrivial finite-Dirichlet steady Stokes solution with zero boundary trace and pressure in L2_loc; the constructed velocity is not a harmonic potential flow.

assumptions.domain: Omega(R0) = H2(-a^2) minus the closed geodesic ball, R0,a > 0

claims.statement: For every R0,a > 0, the same hyperbolic exterior domain admits a nontrivial finite-Dirichlet steady Navier-Stokes solution with zero boundary trace and pressure in L2_loc; the constructed velocity is not a harmonic potential flow.

assumptions.domain: Omega(R0) = H2(-a^2) minus the closed geodesic ball, R0,a > 0

papers.title: Hodge decomposition of the Sobolev space H1 on a space form of nonpositive curvature
papers.version: v1; Differential Geometry and its Applications 2025
papers.scope: H1 Hodge decomposition for k-forms on noncompact nonpositively curved space forms.

claims.statement: The discrete API separates exact, coexact, and harmonic one-form components.
claims.locator: Project FEEC gate motivated by arXiv:1812.11764v1, Theorem 1.3; not a discrete theorem asserted in the paper

claims.statement: For every form degree k on HN(-a^2), a >= 0, H1 k-forms split uniquely and H1-orthogonally into the H1 closures of compactly supported exact and coexact forms plus an L2 harmonic k-form.

assumptions.closures: H1 closures of d Lambda_c^(k-1) and d* Lambda_c^(k+1)
assumptions.harmonic summand: L2 harmonic k-forms, which the paper proves lie in H1
